newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore hopes for bipartisan U.S. policy on Asia.
newsitem.headline: Singapore hopes for bipartisan U.S. policy on Asia.

text.p: Singapore hopes Washington will maintain a consistent focus in its relations with East Asia following Bill Clinton's re-election, a Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
"President Clinton's victory will mean continuity and stability in U.S. foreign policy," she said.
"A stable relationship between (the) U.S. and Japan, China and Southeast Asia will be critical to the continued economic prosperity and political stability in our region," she said.
She added that Singapore also hoped the United States would take a bipartisan approach in its policy towards Asia, she said.

"We are pleased that U.S. policy on continued engagement in Asia was not an issue during the election campaign, and hope that this will mean a bipartisan consensus in policy towards Asia in the next administration."
While Clinton succeeded in retaining the Democrats' hold on the presidency, the Republicans kept control of both houses of Congress.
